messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — private-vpc tenant=NovusHealth — elevated 5xx from tenant-nlb-prod (healthchecks flapping). Paging primary oncall @Eric (oncall). See alert: https://alerts.redwood/1748021111

Eric (oncall): I'm on it. Starting with NLB healthcheck logs + recent deploys. Any customer-facing errors reported by CS?

Tom C. (CSM): NovusHealth just pinged our support line, they see intermittent 502/504 on inbound webhook delivery to their endpoint. They showed a traceroute that times out after our NLB IPs. :eyes:

Maria O'Neill: I see NLB target group healthy_count dropping from 12 -> 2 over last 3 minutes. Healthcheck response codes are 504 and timeouts. No spikes in CPU on the tenant pool hosts though.

Raj Patel: Can someone run a quick curl from one of the tenant pool hosts to the upstream customer endpoint and to 8.8.8.8? Need to rule out egress path.

Jamie I.: Running from host i-0a1b2c3d (tenant-pool-a):
```
$ curl -vS --connect-timeout 5 https://upstream.novushealth.com/health
*   Trying 198.51.100.23:443... connected
* Connected to upstream.novushealth.com (198.51.100.23) port 443 (#0)
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out
```
Also traceroute stalls at our NAT gateway IP 10.254.3.1, looks like conntrack exhaustion maybe.

Kate (SRE Lead): conntrack exhaustion is plausible — we've had tenant egress spikes earlier with similar symptoms. Check conntrack stats and NAT gateway CPU/flows.

Sam R. (eng-relay): Pulling conntrack counts now. On i-0a1b2c3d:
```
# conntrack -S | head -n 5
nf_conntrack count: 65990
nf_conntrack peak: 65000
```
We're above peak and kernel is pruning. That explains sporadic 504s.

Eric (oncall): Okay, triage plan: 1) Temporary mitigation: widen conntrack limit on tenant hosts if safe, 2) Add ephemeral NAT gateway capacity / failover to secondary NAT for this tenant, 3) Execute DNS weight shift + fallback to older NLB if routing impacted. Who can push the conntrack bump?

Maria O'Neill: I can push sysctl immediately across the pool (small risk). Proposed patch: 
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
```
Will roll to 2 hosts first, monitor 1 minute, then rest.

Raj Patel: I'll prepare the NAT gateway failover: spin up standby NAT and attach to the tenant subnet, then update route table to prefer standby (short TTL). ETA ~8-12 min.

Tom C. (CSM): Let me message NovusHealth that we're investigating and implementing mitigation. I'll request they pause any big fan-out jobs for 15m to reduce churn.

Sam R. (eng-relay): One ask: before we change route tables, confirm the standby NAT has the right egress SGs and outbound proxies. We had an issue last quarter where new NAT lacked corporate egress allowlist and got blocked by the customer's WAF.

Jamie I.: Confirmed proxy creds present and SGs match. Also increasing conntrack buys us breathing room for the NAT swap.

Eric (oncall): Maria, please proceed with sysctl on two hosts and report back. Ruby runbook ref: https://runbooks.redwood/private-vpc/conntrack-mitigation

Maria O'Neill: Pushed to host i-0a1b2c3d and i-0d4e5f6g. Watching metrics now. Conntrack count fell to 48k and no new 504s in the last 30s. :white_check_mark:

Kate (SRE Lead): Good. Raj, proceed with NAT failover when ready. Coordinate with Maria for cutover window.

Raj Patel: Standby NAT up and healthy. Kicking route table change to prefer standby, applying weighted route with 80/20 shift for 2 minutes before full switch.

Incident Bot: :information_source: RouteTableChange applied (rtb-0a1) — weight updated.

Tom C. (CSM): NovusHealth confirms fewer errors now, they see delivery success increasing. They're keeping a watch on retry queues.

Eric (oncall): Keep monitoring for 30 minutes. We'll keep conntrack increase in place for now. Need post-incident follow-up: why conntrack spiked — load pattern, retransmit loops, or misbehaving client? Assigning action items:
- Raj: run NAT scaling and audit routing policies for tenant-specific egress resilience.
- Sam: add alert on nf_conntrack nearing 75% of peak for tenant pools.
- Maria: schedule a controlled rollback test and document safe conntrack limits.
- Kate: postmortem owner, link evals to customer impact and runbook improvements.

Kate (SRE Lead): I'll open the incident doc and capture timeline. Tom, please add NovusHealth notes and confirm acceptable mitigation communication.

Tom C. (CSM): Will do. They appreciated the timely updates.

Eric (oncall): Handoff to next oncall @Raj in 18 minutes. If anything flares up, page SRE triage. Otherwise I'll de-escalate after 30m monitoring. :thumbsup:
